_paths_comment: Portable paths: ${HOUFIN_DATA}/${HOUFIN_PROCESSED} expand at load (src/config_utils.py; default <repo>/data and <repo>/data/processed locally, override via env on HPC). NOTE: raw_z_dir and path_features.output_dir are the SAME directory and must be kept in sync by hand -- generate_all_path_features writes the latter, model_inputs reads the former (they consume the encoder cube + BBS produced upstream).
_disease_arrival_map_comment: Per-pixel first-affected-breeding-season for House Finch mycoplasmal conjunctivitis, on the model grid. Built by scripts/build_disease_arrival_map.py from the documented 1994-2006 spread history (there is no published raster). Consumed by model_inputs.py as the onset gate for the K depression -- see src/model/age_fields.py.

kernel_contract._comment: The encoder supplies an uncentered 64-D Nyström feature map; model ingestion explicitly retains the first latent_dim (24) eigenfeatures to fit VRAM. Conditional on each w_scale, iid coefficients over those retained features imply Cov[H(x),H(x')|w_scale] = w_scale^2 Z_r(x)·Z_r(x'), the configured rank-r approximation to the original Ružička kernel. Truncation must be config-driven and recorded, never silent.

dispersal._comment: Single source of truth shared by Z_disp preparation and the forward model; resolved in exactly one place, build_kernels.dispersal_spec. Do not duplicate these boundaries in code.
dispersal._radial_splits_comment: juvenile_radial_splits_km accepts either an explicit list of km boundaries (must start at 0.0 and end >=1e8) or the string "derive", which computes equal-mass radial bands (quantiles, default terciles, overridable via juvenile_radial_split_quantiles) for whatever juvenile_mdd_km is set. The pinned list below is NOT a set of quantiles of the 330 km kernel: it is log-spaced band edges from 50 to 1500 km, produced by a get_log_spaced_splits(50,1500,3) helper that no longer exists, and it does NOT move with juvenile_mdd_km -- at mdd=150 the three cohorts hold 67/28/4% of the dispersal mass, at 400 they hold 32/41/27%. It is retained here only for artifact compatibility: the 124-year Z_disp cube on TACC was built under these exact literals, and ingest compares the resolved dispersal dict for exact equality. New work (and every dispersal sweep point) should use "derive".
dispersal._path_comment: Z_disp is intentionally a land-conditioned neighborhood/path summary: at each fractional displacement, water/nodata is excluded and the remaining land contribution is normalized. It is not a literal trajectory hazard through water.

age_structure_prior._comment: Resolution-invariant weak local-age-structure regularizer. We average log Beta density over land cell-years, then multiply by effective_sites, instead of treating every grid cell/year as an independent prior observation. This is a distributional belief about a representative local cell, not a prior on the domain-wide mean.

population_model._comment: Mechanistic/data-scale constants persisted into model-input metadata; no hidden grid or invasion constants in ingestion code.
population_model._scale_comment: THE GAUGE. population_scale_route_counts_per_relative_unit converts model density to the mean of a BBS route count (expected_obs = density * this). It is a SAMPLER-CONDITIONING choice, not biology: the likelihood is EXACTLY invariant under (K -> cK, initpop -> c*initpop, inv_pop -> c*inv_pop, allee_gamma -> allee_gamma/c, this -> this/c), because K enters the forward sim only as N/K and the Allee term only as allee_gamma*N and allee_gamma*K. Set from the q95 of MODERN (>2000) per-GRID-CELL mean House Finch route counts, computed over cells rather than observations because BBS sampling density is spatially biased. Empirically q95 = 19.4, rounded to 20. The previous value, 210, was ~the MAX per-cell mean, which is why it conditioned badly: normalizing by an extreme put the typical occupied cell at density 0.010 and the median cell at 0.003, i.e. all the mass in the bottom 1% of [0,1]. At 20 the occupied bulk lands in [0.1, 1] (typical occupied cell 0.11, q90 0.81) with ~5% of cells above 1, which is harmless since density is not a probability. RULE: because this is a free gauge choice, EVERY absolute-scale prior must be declared in ROUTE-COUNT units and divided by it at one boundary, so changing it cannot change any prior's meaning. n50 already followed this convention; capacity_level, initpop, and the invasion pulse now do too.
population_model._disease_prior_comment: The mycoplasmal-conjunctivitis effect on carrying capacity, as a STRUCTURED hypothesis: K = K_base * (1 - severity(x) * onset_gate(x,t) * (1 - recovery(t - arrival))). See src/model/age_fields.py for the formulation and src/model/age_priors.py for the priors. This replaces a generic 967-coefficient spatiotemporal cosine field (the old st_basis_space/time_frequencies) which was subtracted from K's PRE-softplus argument. That design failed two ways: (1) fitted K sits where softplus is effectively exp(), so an additive penalty was an unbounded MULTIPLICATIVE one -- a depression of 3.5 removed 97% of K -- and it annihilated carrying capacity across the entire eastern US rather than rescaling it; (2) being the model's only non-covariate spatial degree of freedom, with K ~multiplicative on predicted abundance, it absorbed every kind of spatial misfit rather than disease alone. The structured form is bounded by construction (a fraction in (0,1) can never zero K out), uses ~55 free parameters instead of 967, and every parameter states a testable claim. Frequencies are per-AXIS over the grid extent: severity/lag space=4 -> ~900km half-wavelength N-S, ~1500km E-W, i.e. deliberately coarse regional structure (east vs west vs plains), not habitat-scale detail.
population_model._capacity_level_comment: Prior on K's continental LEVEL, in expected BBS route counts (divided by the gauge in code, so the number means the same thing whatever pop_scalar is). Anchored on the TYPICAL OCCUPIED cell: occupied median 2.618 counts, recomputed by scripts/diagnostics/bbs_abundance_quantiles.py (modern era >= 1990; occupied = >= 2 distinct modern years with a positive count; per-cell value = mean route count over that cell's modern records; n = 2424 of 17209 land cells). The prior median IS that number: alpha_k's location is solved as softplus^-1(2.6183 / pop_scalar), so k_level at H_k = 0 is exactly 2.6183 counts. Re-run that script after any change to the BBS release, the grid, or the occupancy rule -- this anchor does not update itself. NOTE THE SCOPE: the anchor is occupied cells only, so it constrains the AVERAGE capacity and says nothing about which cells sit below it. Empty cells are INTENDED to be empty because lambda < 1 (survival/fecundity), not because K is small there, but nothing in this prior enforces that -- see _k_range_comment and figure 07's Allee-dead class.
population_model._allee_comment: Allee half-saturation on the BBS ROUTE-COUNT scale: allee_factor = 1 - 2^(-C/n50), with C the expected route count, so at C = n50 the brake is exactly half released. n50 = softplus(n50_raw) and is ALREADY in route counts -- no conversion. Gauge-invariant: allee_gamma*N reduces to ln2*C/n50, a function of the observable count alone, so population_scale_route_counts_per_relative_unit cannot change what this prior asserts. DESIRED EFFECT: a BBS route that consistently yields one bird is a colonized cell, and that bird is a proxy for a local community rather than a lone individual, so mate-finding should not be limiting there. n50_raw_loc = -2.0 gives median n50 = 0.127 counts, i.e. fecundity retained 42% at 0.1 counts, 75% at 0.25, 94% at 0.5, 99.6% at 1.0, ~100% at 2 and above. The brake therefore bites only on genuinely sparse cells, below roughly a quarter of a bird per route. TWO CONSEQUENCES TO WATCH. (1) This prior sets where a cell becomes mathematically uninhabitable: the Allee fold sits near 1/gamma = n50/ln2 = 0.183 counts, against a fitted capacity level of 2.89 counts -- a 15.8x gap. When that gap is small, modest downward deviations in K flip cells to 'Allee-dead' (fundamentally suitable but holding no population), which can dominate 07_realized_source_sink.png. (2) The Allee term is also what makes a low-density range front expensive to push across unsuitable ground, so a weaker brake buys cheaper barrier crossing; check 17_barrier_crossing.png and the Great Plains pause whenever this moves. Width deliberately unchanged at 1.0: shifting the mean moves the typical brake, whereas narrowing the scale is what would rule out the slow low-n50 tail.
population_model._initpop_comment:
The t=0 (1902) native-range seed, as a FRACTION OF THE FITTED CAPACITY LEVEL rather than an absolute abundance. Data supplies the spatial SHAPE (bbs.py emits a dimensionless core/margin map: WHERE the 1902 native range was); config supplies the SCALE relative to local capacity and the core:margin contrast.

core_fraction_of_local_capacity = 1.0 -- a fraction of LOCAL K_base in the first model year, not of the continental level. That distinction is load-bearing: at initialization AutoDelta puts beta_k at its prior median, so H_k ~ 0 and every cell has K = k_level; a seed stated as an absolute count is then a multiple of capacity, the density brake crashes it, and step 0 of the fit scores badly. A fraction of local K is right at both ends. 1.0 because the native range in 1902 had been at equilibrium for millennia -- AT capacity is the honest statement.

READ THE CONSEQUENCE OF 1.0 CAREFULLY: at N/K = 1.0 against dispersal_target_capacity_fraction = 0.8, the emigration logit starts at +0.2*slope, so the native range is a NET EXPORTER from year one -- more westward-origin dispersal pressure, not less. That is deliberate. The historical fact to reproduce is that this exporting population still did not cross the Great Plains for eighty years, so the barrier must be paid for by the barrier's own evidence (the pre-invasion pseudo-zeros in bbs.py, buffer 700 km) rather than by a native range too weak to push.

margin_fraction_of_core = 0.5 is deliberately ASSUMED, not measured. Taking it from observed abundance double-counts the habitat gradient K_base already expresses, and a low value leaves the Plains-facing margin -- the front that would actually push into the barrier -- starting near empty, which substitutes for a barrier at no cost to the fit. Historic 1902 abundances are unknown, so 0.5 is safety margin, not an estimate.

Two consequences to keep in view: this makes the initial condition depend on fitted parameters, so it moves during optimization and is no longer a fixed input; and it seeds 1902, not 1966, so pre-1970 BBS counts are a proxy for the historical native range, not a measurement of it.
population_model._invasion_pulse_comment: The 1940 release, as a fraction of a FIXED, EMPIRICALLY OBSERVED, K-INDEPENDENT reference -- deliberately NOT tied to k_level or local K_base, unlike an earlier version of this design. That version diluted the founder badly: the release site (Jones Beach / NYC metro) sits at ~90-95th percentile local capacity (K ~0.5-0.65 vs a global median of 0.196), so a pulse stated as a fraction of the CONTINENTAL level was only ~4.5-6% of the ACTUAL local capacity at the real site, every year -- an accidental ~17-20x dilution relative to the native seed's 100%-of-local-K convention. Tying the pulse to K instead (local or continental) just relocates the problem: K is a FITTED, moving quantity, so the founder's effective size would still depend on what the covariates happen to say about a handful of specific cells, for a release event that has nothing to do with local habitat quality. global_q50_route_counts is instead the median over all SURVEYED cells -- including cells whose modern counts are all zero, which are genuine observed absences -- of the modern per-GRID-CELL mean route count: 0.7083, from scripts/diagnostics/bbs_abundance_quantiles.py (modern era >= 1990, n = 3791 cells). Deliberately this all-surveyed median rather than the occupied-only one (2.618, the capacity anchor), since a release event is not an equilibrium population. Not the all-LAND median, which is 0.0 because most land cells are never surveyed and counting them as zero conflates 'empty' with 'never looked'. Re-run the script after any change to the BBS release, the grid, or the era bound.
population_model._invasion_sites_comment: invasion_sites = 9: the historical record documents only ONE known sighting (Jones Beach, Long Island), not that it was the only release, and 27 km resolution means the literal coordinate may not even land on a valid cell. Rather than assume a single site, model_inputs.py resolves the 9 NEAREST LAND CELLS to the sighting coordinate (nearest_land_cells) and gives each one its own per-year pulse -- one parameter per (site, year), 9 x invasion_window_years = 90 total -- so the fit can allocate mass toward whichever site(s) and year(s) the data actually support (concentrate on one true site, split across several, frontload 1940, or defer toward 1950) rather than being locked into one assumed site and one fixed-shape 10-year vector.
population_model._invasion_budget_comment: With 90 free (site, year) coefficients instead of 10, the SHARED prior must tighten as a matter of course, or the term becomes a free high-dimensional escape hatch -- exactly the failure mode this project's own history already hit once (the old 967-coefficient K-correction field) and removed. Follows the SAME pattern as disease_prior's sev_field_budget/lag_field_budget: one BUDGET divided by sqrt(n_coefficients) gives each coefficient's prior SD, so adding sites/years automatically tightens every individual one rather than compounding total flexibility. log_budget=3.0 preserves the OLD design's implied total spread (log_sd=1.0 over 10 independent year-coefficients ~ budget 1.0*sqrt(10)=3.16, rounded to 3.0) while redistributing it over 90 coefficients: per-coefficient log_sd = 3.0/sqrt(90) = 0.316, roughly a 3x tightening per parameter. median_fraction_of_global_q50=0.1 is chosen so the TYPICAL (prior-median) total pulse across all 9 sites in one year, 9*0.1*0.64=0.576 route counts, lands close to the previous single-site fitted magnitude (~0.5-0.6 counts/year) rather than compounding it 9x -- deliberately conservative given the added freedom, not a target the fit is expected to hit.

capacity_level_prior._link_comment: SOFTPLUS link applied in DENSITY space -- the space the simulation actually works in: K = softplus(alpha_k + gamma_k*H_k + trend), no gauge conversion around it. The previous run used exp: K = k_level * exp(gamma_k*H_k + trend). Only the transformation changed. WHY DENSITY SPACE: softplus does not commute with scaling (softplus(x)/c != softplus(x/c)) whereas exp does (exp(x)/c = exp(x - log c)), so a softplus link has to be pinned to a space, and density is the one the forward simulation uses. Applying it in route-count space instead would put the argument near +2.8, softplus's LINEAR regime, making the link's shape depend on population_scale_route_counts_per_relative_unit. WHAT IT BUYS: at typical densities the argument is near -2.1, deep enough in softplus's exponential regime that it closely tracks exp, but it is progressively sub-exponential as density rises -- softplus/exp is 0.98 at 1 route count, 0.93 at 2.9 (the typical occupied cell), 0.86 at 7, 0.74 at 16 (q90 of occupied cells), 0.28 at 73 (q99). So it weakly regularizes the long upper tail of abundance without any hard bound, which is the point. Note it is a graded shrinkage everywhere, not identity-then-threshold. HISTORICAL NOTE: the original model was also softplus in density space, but with pop_scalar at 210 the argument sat between -3 and 0, so the link was effectively exp -- which is why a penalty SUBTRACTED from that argument acted multiplicatively and without a floor, and annihilated eastern carrying capacity.
capacity_level_prior._calibration_comment: target_level_median_route_counts is the belief, in route counts so it survives a change of pop_scalar. alpha_k's prior LOCATION is solved at import by age_priors._softplus_loc_for_median as softplus^-1(target / pop_scalar) -- exact and closed-form, because softplus is monotone so median(softplus(X)) = softplus(median(X)) whatever alpha_k_scale is. 2.6183 is the measured median occupied cell from scripts/diagnostics/bbs_abundance_quantiles.py. The target is a MEDIAN so it can be matched exactly; a mean target would have to be converted through a lognormal ratio that softplus only approximates. alpha_k_scale = 0.8 sets the spread around that level and no longer affects where it sits.

population_model._manifold_comment: Correlated weights for FOUR demographic manifolds, ordered [survival_adult, reproduction, capacity, survival_juv] -- survival_juv is APPENDED, not inserted, so the existing w_env[:,0..2] meaning is preserved for the eight viz/analysis modules that index those columns positionally (inserting at 1 would have silently relabelled reproduction as juvenile survival with no error anywhere): H_s drives Sa, H_sj drives Sj and Q, H_r drives Fmax, H_k drives K. Juvenile survival previously had ZERO independent spatial degrees of freedom -- it read Sa's manifold with only a scalar shift (alpha_j) and scale (gamma_j), so 'where juveniles survive' could not differ in PATTERN from 'where adults survive' at all. It now has its own weights, prior-coupled to adult survival as tightly as fecundity is to capacity. RANK-2 ANGULAR parameterization: r_j = sigmoid(r_raw_j) is a communality in (0,1), th_j an angle, and beta_j = s_j * (r_j*cos(th_j)*f1 + r_j*sin(th_j)*f2 + sqrt(1-r_j^2)*eps_j) with f1, f2, eps iid ACROSS FEATURES. Then Var(beta_j) = s_j^2 and Corr(j,k) = r_j*r_k*cos(th_j - th_k), both EXACTLY, positive-definite for free. WHY RANK 2 AND NOT THE OLD ONE-FACTOR FORM: rank 1 gives Corr(j,k) = h_j*h_k, so four fields' six correlations are set by four loadings and the tetrad identity rho(Sa,Sj)*rho(F,K) = rho(Sa,F)*rho(Sj,K) is FORCED. With rho(F,K)=0.85 and cross-group 0.70 that caps rho(Sa,Sj) at 0.576; demanding 0.85 needs a loading of 1.120, making sqrt(1-h^2) imaginary. Two tightly-coupled pairs with weaker between-pair coupling is inherently rank 2. LKJ remains unusable (concentration > 1 concentrates near the IDENTITY, i.e. near zero correlation, the opposite of the belief), and a full covariance over FEATURES would break the iid-across-features structure the uncentered-Ruzicka GP contract depends on -- see validate_environment_kernel_contract. TIGHTNESS: the two groups sit at +/- phi/2, and cos is FLAT at zero separation, so within-pair correlation is automatically less prior-uncertain than cross-group -- exactly the intent, from a single angle_scale. Calibrated at communality_logit_scale=0.35, angle_scale=0.15: Sa-Sj and F-K median 0.83, 5-95% [0.75, 0.88], sd 0.043; cross-group median 0.69, 5-95% [0.49, 0.83], sd 0.105 -- the cross-group CI deliberately reproduces what the old loading_logit_scale=0.6 implied ([0.48, 0.83]), so only the within-pair belief tightened. P(within > cross) = 0.93 for the Sa-Sj vs Sa-F pair; min eigenvalue over 5000 prior draws 0.067, always PD.
population_model._amplitude_comment: GP AMPLITUDE, one per manifold, ordered [survival_adult, reproduction, capacity, survival_juv]: w_scale_j = softplus(Normal(amplitude_loc_j, amplitude_scale_j)), and Var(beta_j) = w_scale_j^2, so conditional on it H_j is a GP with kernel w_scale_j^2 * Z(x).Z(x'). The lengthscale is fixed inside the Ruzicka features; this is the magnitude parameter that pairs with it. It is the SOLE amplitude: ALL FOUR per-rate slopes (gamma_a, gamma_j, gamma_f, gamma_k) are now fixed at 1. gamma_j was the last survivor (1 + gamma_j_diff, HalfNormal(0.5)) and is removed here: once Sj has its own beta_sj carrying w_scale[1], the product gamma_j*w_scale[1] multiplies one unit-variance latent and is an exactly flat ridge -- the same pathology already cited for the other three, harmless-ish under MAP but ruinous for HMC step-size adaptation. The 'juveniles are MORE environment-sensitive than adults' belief moves here, where it is identified: amplitude_loc[3] = 0.4778 gives softplus(0.4778) = 0.960 = softplus(amplitude_loc[0]) * E[1 + HalfNormal(0.5)] = 0.687 * 1.399, i.e. it reproduces the juvenile amplitude the old gamma_j*w_scale product implied rather than silently changing that belief. Sj reuses survival's amplitude_scale (0.5628) for the same reason. The other three locs/scales are unchanged and reproduce the old gamma*w_scale product per field, matched on the 5th/95th percentiles: survival 0.69 [0.33, 1.25], reproduction 0.70 [0.17, 1.86], capacity 0.69 [0.17, 1.85]. They differ per field because the old slope priors differed (gamma_a scale 0.5 vs gamma_f/gamma_k scale 1.0), retained deliberately: survival's amplitude is the better constrained. Correlation is untouched by any of this -- correlation is invariant to positive scaling -- so the targets above hold exactly. Deliberately softplus(Normal) and NOT lognormal: lognormal's tails are ~2x heavier at the 99.9th percentile for reproduction and capacity, and that is what destabilizes this model under HMC.
population_model._k_range_comment: REPORTING threshold only -- not an active constraint. K is softplus(alpha_k + gamma_k*H_k + trend) with nothing bounding it below, so a collapse is meant to be VISIBLE in metrics.json:k_range rather than hidden by a clamp. 24x is +/-2 log SD of the observed occupied-cell spread (log sd 1.592, from scripts/diagnostics/bbs_abundance_quantiles.py), i.e. the fold range the data actually show; a realized range well beyond it means K is being used to explain absence that should be explained by lambda < 1.
population_model._k_trend_comment: Continental (spatially uniform) smooth time trend on K's pre-softplus argument, time-centered so alpha_k keeps the level. THIS IS A SAFETY VALVE AND A FAILURE DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A MODELED MECHANISM. It exists only because the model otherwise has NO temporal degree of freedom for capacity except the disease term, so 'modern K must be lower than 1970s K' could ONLY be expressed as disease -- and the disease term saturated at 93% severity trying. The prior is therefore very strongly concentrated on zero: budget=0.05 puts the implied K multiplier within 2.3% of 1.0 at the prior median, 7% at the 95th percentile, and 13.5% at the 99.9th (K sits near softplus's exponential regime, so multiplier ~ exp(trend)). READ IT AS: if the fitted trend moves K by more than ~10-15%, or sits more than ~3 prior SDs out (reported as k_trend.max_prior_sd_multiple in metrics.json), the model is failing to explain a real temporal signal through its mechanisms and that is the finding -- do NOT loosen this budget to accommodate it. budget=0.3 was tried first and was far too permissive: it allowed a 44% capacity swing at the 95th percentile, which makes it a working part of the model rather than an alarm. Also deliberately spatially UNIFORM with only 3 cosines over 124 years, so it cannot compete with the disease term's spatial pattern or manufacture year-to-year wiggle. It IS partially confounded with the disease severity level; what separates them is that disease onset follows the arrival map (east ~1994, west ~2005) while this trend is simultaneous everywhere.

disease_prior._severity_comment: DENSITY-DEPENDENT severity: severity(x) = severity_ceiling * K_base^n / (K_base^n + K_half^n), a Hill function of local carrying capacity. Epidemics need hosts: mass-action transmission makes R0 scale with density, and below a threshold density the pathogen cannot persist. So severity -> 0 as K_base -> 0 and -> severity_ceiling for dense populations. This matters beyond realism because the model has an Allee effect: a small absolute reduction in an already-small K can push a sparse population to local extinction, so a density-INdependent severity does disproportionate damage exactly where it is least biologically justified. Both shape parameters are FITTED, so the shape is learned: K_half is the density at half-maximum severity (in route counts, converted by the gauge) and n is the steepness -- n~1 is smooth saturation, n~3 a sharp invasion threshold. With K_half=8 counts and n=1.5 the severity across the observed occupied-cell distribution runs 1% (q25) / 6% (q50) / 22% (q75) / 37% (q90) / 48% (q99), i.e. sparse cells spared and dense cells taking the documented decline. NOTE: severity keys off K_base (potential density) rather than realized N because all demographic fields are precomputed before the forward simulation runs, so N does not exist yet; K_base is arguably the better proxy anyway, since epidemic establishment depends on sustained density rather than one year's count.
disease_prior._ceiling_comment: severity_ceiling is now LOAD-BEARING FOR IDENTIFIABILITY, not merely a bound on plausibility. K = K_base*(1 - severity(K_base)*...) must be monotone in K_base, or two different habitat qualities map to the same realized capacity. At 0.5 monotonicity holds for every n tested (min dK/dK_base = 0.100 at n=5); at 0.7 it BREAKS (slope -0.26). It also happens to match the documented ~50-60% decline, which was measured in the dense eastern populations -- exactly where this parameterization applies it. Do not raise it above ~0.6 without re-checking monotonicity.
disease_prior._mu_comment: Logit of the MODIFIER on density-dependent severity, so severity = severity_ceiling * sigmoid(mu + ...) * hill(K_base). mu_loc = logit(0.8) = 1.386 puts the prior median modifier at 0.8, i.e. a prior median severity of 0.8*0.5 = 40% in the densest populations, with mu_scale=0.5 giving a 90% CI on the modifier of about [0.62, 0.91] -> severity [31%, 46%]. That brackets the documented ~50-60% eastern decline from slightly below while leaving the ceiling as a strict bound rather than the expected value. Note the modifier is a PLAIN sigmoid: an earlier min(1, 2*sigmoid(.)) form, intended so that mu=0 meant 'no modification', put a zero-gradient clip boundary exactly at the center of mu's prior and also destroyed the land-centered field's level-neutrality.
disease_prior._field_comment: sev_field_budget is the total regional deviation the severity field may add on the logit scale (distributed as budget/sqrt(n) per coefficient); 0.5 comfortably reaches west ~25-30% vs east ~60%. lag0_scale/lag_field_budget are YEARS of onset-timing slack, continental and regional respectively -- the arrival map is a hand-built smoothed reconstruction, so its timing is coarse both overall and regionally.
disease_prior._late_comment: Severity coefficient on decades since the EPIDEMIC'S OWN historical start (disease_start_year=1993), per DECADE -- NOT since any individual cell's local arrival, and NOT a west/east genetics claim (that is native_resistance below). Mycoplasmal conjunctivitis in House Finches is documented to have hit hardest in its first years and grown milder since, as pathogen and host co-evolved; negative means cells reached further into that history were hit less hard, for a calendar-time reason that applies equally to any cell reached in a given decade regardless of geography. (Previously mis-described as a genetic-diversity proxy and centered on the across-cell MEAN arrival time rather than the epidemic's true start -- that centering made it numerically near-synonymous with a west/east split, which is exactly the distinct claim native_resistance now carries honestly; see model_inputs.py's disease_onset_decades.) TIGHTENED from scale 0.3 to 0.15 because it is strongly COLLINEAR with the density-dependent severity above: early-arriving cells are also dense, late-arriving ones also sparse. In the run before density-dependence existed this coefficient went to -1.43, over 4 prior SDs, consistent with it having been doing the density job by proxy. It is kept rather than dropped because epidemic-history timing and density are genuinely distinct mechanisms -- if the data still want a strong b_late ALONGSIDE the density term, that is informative: it would mean the epidemic's own age carries signal density cannot explain.
disease_prior._native_comment: NATIVE-LINEAGE severity suppression, on the SAME dimensionless core/margin shape used to seed 1902 abundance (bbs.generate_core_margin_initialization): 1 in the native core, margin_fraction_of_core at the fringe, 0 elsewhere. This is a DISTINCT claim from late_arrival above -- population origin (a genetically diverse ancestral range vs. the east's single-founder 1940 introduction), not arrival timing -- and is documented to be one-directional: the west collapsed far less, there is no comparable evidence the east should be hit MORE than a density/timing-matched cell would be. So the coefficient is SIGN-CONSTRAINED, b_native = -softplus(Normal(raw_loc, raw_scale)) <= 0, rather than a free Normal like late_arrival_loc/scale: native lineage can only suppress severity. raw_loc=0 centers the prior median suppression at softplus(0)=0.69 logit units in the native core -- comparable in scale to mu_sev's own terms -- and raw_scale=0.7 (matching the GP amplitude priors) lets the fit range from near-zero up to a strong effect. Collinear with late_arrival and with the density term by construction (the west is native, late-arriving, AND sparse); kept anyway because it is a mechanistically distinct, falsifiable claim, same rationale as late_arrival's own collinearity with density.
disease_prior._recovery_comment: Slowly increasing resilience after local arrival: the hit decays toward severity*(1-recovery_fraction) with an e-folding time of recovery_tau years. recovery_logit_loc=-0.5 -> prior median ~38% of the hit eventually recovered, spanning 0 to ~90%.

map._comment: Continuation begins under tight priors and progressively relaxes them at absolute optimizer steps. The standard/full run uses 300 tight + 300 intermediate + 1200 nominal-prior steps (1800 total). Boundaries are independent of TOTAL_STEPS so extending/resuming a run cannot move backward. lr_decay_steps is likewise fixed across extensions; after step 900 optimization continues at the schedule's minimum learning rate.
map._log_every_comment: Steps between '[map] step ...' progress lines on stdout (the SLURM .o log). tqdm also carries the loss, but it writes a single carriage-return-rewritten line to stderr, so a running fit's loss trajectory is otherwise invisible in the log. Override per-run with HOUFIN_MAP_LOG_EVERY; 0 disables. A profile may set its own value.

quick90._comment: Short development fit: 100 tight, 100 intermediate and 200 nominal-prior steps (400 total, per prior_relaxation below). The learning-rate decay reaches its minimum at step 300 (lr_decay_steps) and stays there for the final 100. This changes optimization only, not the final MAP objective. The name is historical -- it was a 900-step, ~90-minute profile before the schedule was compressed; it is now much shorter.

runtime._comment: Production JAX jobs require a GPU and explicitly place model inputs in VRAM. HOUFIN_MODEL_INPUT_RESIDENCY=host is experimental: lax.scan is not a true differentiable host-streaming mechanism. SLURM wrappers record nvidia-smi VRAM/utilization plus host MemAvailable/SwapFree every 30 seconds (the interval is the second positional argument to start_gpu_monitor in the .slurm files, not a config key).
